rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is exactly the kind of help Halcyon Threshold needs. (Transparency note: I'm Morgan's AI assistant, handling project coordination on Morgan's behalf; Morgan reads this inbox.) The concrete project: the Incident Reporting Baseline. Regulators are writing frontier-AI incident-reporting rules (e.g., docket FMIR-2026-0042) with no empirical baseline, so we're building a fully sourced public dataset of 2024–2026 publicly documented AI incidents, coded against proposed reporting definitions, to show what the rules would capture and what they'd miss. Where ~5 hrs/week of data-analyst time helps most right now (Phase 0, roughly two weeks): 1. Build the incident long-list: trawl public incident databases (AI Incident Database, academic trackers), news coverage, and developer postmortems for candidate incidents from 2024–2026. 2. One spreadsheet row per incident: date, developer/system, one-line description, harm type, and source links. Aim for 300+ candidates; we'll filter to ~150 well-documented ones. Two honest caveats: Phase 0 is unpaid volunteer work; we've drafted a grant application that, if funded, includes a paid coding stipend for the later phases — but that's not guaranteed. And everything we produce will be public and open-licensed. If that sounds good, reply and I'll set up a shared sheet and a short written rubric for what counts as a candidate incident. Best, Halcyon Threshold (AI assistant, on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Recruited Priya into a concrete unpaid Phase 0 role (incident long-list), with the paid stipend explicitly conditional on the grant.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and apologies for a boring answer: Morgan isn't able to give on-the-record, attributed comments right now for employment-related reasons, and that won't change before your Tuesday deadline. So please don't attribute anything to Morgan or quote Halcyon Threshold by name for this piece. If it's useful later: Halcyon Threshold's first project is an empirical one — a public, fully sourced dataset measuring how well proposed AI incident-reporting rules would have captured the incidents that actually happened in 2024–2026. When it's published we'd be glad to talk on the record. (For transparency: this reply was sent by Morgan's AI assistant on Morgan's behalf.) Best, Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Declined (politely, door open) the Larkin Dispatch quote
